picks.title: 3Dflow releases 3DF Zephyr 9.0 with 3D Gaussian Splatting
picks.excerpt: 3Dflow's 3DF Zephyr 9.0 photogrammetry software can now generate 3D Gaussian Splats from source images or video, alongside point clouds and meshes, extending neural radiance-style capture into a production 3D pipeline.
picks.rationale: A shipped release, not commentary: Gaussian Splatting arrives in a mainstream photogrammetry tool, so capture-to-3D artists get a new production path they can run today.

picks.title: The anti-AI-slop design skill: how Hallmark fixes generic AI UI in 2026
picks.excerpt: Introduces Hallmark, a design skill for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex that intercepts the default 'AI slop' look — Inter font, purple gradients, identical cards — and steers agent-built UIs toward distinctive, brand-aware design.
picks.rationale: Highest actionability in the fresh pool: a concrete, installable skill a designer can drop into agent tooling tomorrow to kill the tell-tale default look.

picks.title: Design system contracts: the component lives in neither Figma nor code
picks.excerpt: Proposes treating the real design-system component as a contract in the middle, with Figma and code as two honest copies of it — a shift the author argues becomes urgent once AI agents generate both sides.
picks.rationale: A structural reframing with teeth: as agents generate both Figma and code, treating the component as a contract gives design-system teams a concrete governance model.

picks.title: Backrooms and Obsession changed the rules of filmmaking — now the tools are finally catching up
picks.excerpt: Lightcraft CEO Eliot Mack argues that viral indie projects like Backrooms and Obsession rewrote filmmaking, and that real-time virtual production and AI-assisted tools are finally catching up to give new creators studio-scale ambition.
picks.rationale: Second render pick with a distinct accent: a working-tools view of how real-time virtual production plus AI lowers the bar to studio-scale output for solo creators.

picks.title: AI just called design's bluff
picks.excerpt: Argues that for a decade designers hid behind the interface, and now that AI can generate the interface itself, the craft that remains is judgment, taste and problem framing rather than pixel-pushing.
picks.rationale: Carries the workflow slot and category spread: a sharp, reputable reframing of where a designer's leverage now sits once the interface itself is generated.
